_comment: Tier-2 for fenics biharmonic#0: the C0 interior-penalty rule of thumb alpha = 4*(k+1)^2 is a STABILITY floor, not an accuracy optimum, and an under-penalised scheme does not diverge under refinement — it converges from a blown-up constant. Wrong variant: taking alpha = 4*(k+1)^2 = 36 for P2 as "the" value. Right variant: alpha = 1, which on this problem is stable and roughly six times more accurate. C0-IP MMS on the unit square, u = sin(pi x) sin(pi y), simply supported, P2, N = 8 / 16 / 32, L2 error. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 on dolfinx 0.10.0 / basix 0.10.0 (conda env `fenics`, real scalars); every expect_in_output string was copied from that run. T2_MUTATE=1 removes the pathology and the fixture then fails its own expectations.
